newsitem.title: INDIA: India considering free coffee imports -agency.
newsitem.headline: India considering free coffee imports -agency.

text.p: India is considering to allow free coffee imports to stabilise domestic prices, the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted senior government officials as saying on Monday.
PTI quoted the highest-ranking civil servant in the Commerce Ministry P.P. Prabhu as saying that allowing free imports would be the most viable solution to stabilise prices.
Prabhu said the government was also considering to impose an export duty and put a ceiling on coffee exports.
India, which exports bulk of its coffee, has freed coffee trade from the five decade old marketing controls in the last four years. It allows free exports of coffee but does not permit imports.
Traders said substantial coffee imports would not take place even if the government allowed free imports as international prices were ruling high.
"Global prices are so high," Navin Bopapya, an official in a leading coffee export firm, told Reuters. "Who will import coffee."
PTI quoted chairman of the state-run Coffee Board Philipose Mathai as saying that the solution to control domestic prices was somehwere between a levy on exports and a ceiling on exports.
Mathai said the Coffee Board was preparing a report after the recent spurt in global and domestic prices. It would submit its recommendations to the government in a fortnight.
